meta.title: TuneSync — Your music, all in one place
meta.description: Connect WebDAV, Plex, Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin, Emby, Synology Audio Station, or local folders. Browse and play one library, keep listening with infinite playback and smooth transitions, follow synced lyrics, separate vocals, and record, mix, and share your own takes.

home.headline: <lead>Your music,</lead><accent>all in one place</accent>
home.subhead: Connect WebDAV, Plex, Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin, Emby, Synology Audio Station, or local folders. TuneSync brings everything into one library, keeps playing with infinite playback and smooth transitions, follows synced lyrics, and lets you separate vocals to sing, record, and mix your own take.
home.introTitle: Music shouldn't be spread across half a dozen apps.
home.introBody: TuneSync brings your servers, folders, and player together. Connect once and start listening while the rest of your library fills in.
home.downloadSubtitle: TuneSync is on the App Store for iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Core library browsing and everyday playback are free; TuneSync Plus adds advanced karaoke, lyrics, metadata, analysis, and discovery.
home.downloadIOSAria: Open the iOS getting started guide

ios.label: iPhone / iPad / Mac
ios.desc: One native app with layouts that adapt to iPhone, iPhone Duo, iPad, and Mac. Connect a server, organize your library, and play.

android.label: Android
android.desc: There is no Android version today; TuneSync is focused on Apple platforms.

windows.label: Windows
windows.desc: Windows is not planned right now; the focus is on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

quote1.text: I used to switch between several apps to play my own music. After connecting the NAS, everything is in one place.
quote1.author: Lin Yifan

quote2.text: Infinite playback quietly tops up the queue with similar tracks, and the crossfade keeps the music going without gaps.
quote2.author: M. Chen

quote3.text: I didn't expect to remove vocals and sing on my phone. Lower the original vocal, sing along, then open Audio Studio to mix the take.
quote3.author: Kai

quote4.text: My library info was fairly disorganized. Comparing file tags with MusicBrainz and iTunes let me choose exactly which fields to fill in.
quote4.author: Zhang Rui

quote5.text: The iPad layout gives the lyrics their own space, and the beat-reactive background is a nice touch without being distracting.
quote5.author: D. Wang

quote6.text: It found my server on the LAN and connected after a quick setup — easier than I expected.
quote6.author: Eric

home.ctaTitle: Connect your music and start listening.
home.ctaBody: Add a server or a local folder and press play — artwork and metadata fill in while you listen.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: One library, endless listening, and a studio for your own takes — all in one app.

library.title: Library
library.desc: Songs, albums, artists, and playlists from every connected source, searchable in one place.
library.featureTitle: One library for all your music
library.featureDesc: Browse by song, album, artist, or playlist, or search the whole library. TuneSync starts playing as soon as folders are added, and artwork and metadata keep filling in while you listen.
library.featureB1: Browse songs, albums, artists, and playlists
library.featureB3: Play while indexing continues in the background
library.featureB4: Artwork and metadata fill in gradually

sources.title: Your sources
sources.desc: WebDAV, Plex, Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin, Emby, Synology Audio Station, and local folders.
sources.featureTitle: Connect the music you already own
sources.featureDesc: Add a WebDAV server, pick a music server, or import local folders. TuneSync indexes only the folders you choose, and playback starts right away while artwork and metadata keep filling in.
sources.featureB1: WebDAV over HTTPS, plus local music folders
sources.featureB3: Synology Audio Station and folder-level indexing

player.title: Playback
player.desc: Lossless playback, infinite queue, smooth transitions, and a player that moves with the beat.
player.featureTitle: Keep listening, without reaching for your phone
player.featureDesc: Play FLAC, ALAC, and the rest of your library with background audio and a full queue. Infinite playback refills the queue with similar tracks as it runs low, and smooth transitions blend songs with a 1, 3, 5, or 8-second crossfade. The full-screen player takes its color from the artwork and can follow beats detected on device.
player.featureB1: FLAC, ALAC, and common formats with background playback
player.featureB2: Infinite playback refills the queue automatically

lyrics.title: Lyrics & karaoke
lyrics.desc: Synced or static lyrics with adjustable size and motion; one tap into sing mode.
lyrics.featureTitle: Follow every line, then switch to singing
lyrics.featureDesc: Lyrics scroll in time with the song with the current line highlighted, or stay still as plain text. Adjust text size and motion to suit you, then tap the mic to separate vocals and backing tracks — on device, or with an optional configured cloud service.
lyrics.featureB1: Synced or static lyrics with adjustable text size
lyrics.featureB2: Optional motion that follows beats detected on device
lyrics.featureB3: Vocal separation on device or via an optional cloud service
lyrics.featureB4: One tap from lyrics into sing mode

karaoke.title: Sing & record
karaoke.desc: Lower the original vocal, sing with the accompaniment, and record your take in sync.
karaoke.featureTitle: Your take, recorded in time with the song
karaoke.featureDesc: Once the split is ready, lower the original vocal and keep the accompaniment. Sing along with the lyrics while the microphone records your voice, mixed with input/output latency compensation so everything stays aligned. A failed cloud separation can be cancelled and retried without leaving the player.
karaoke.featureB4: Cancel and retry a failed separation in place

audioStudio.title: Audio Studio
audioStudio.desc: Mix, trim, and punch in on real waveforms; compare Edited with Original.
audioStudio.featureTitle: Shape a take into the version worth keeping
audioStudio.featureDesc: Open a saved recording in Audio Studio. Balance vocal and backing, trim the keep range, or punch in a section. Choose Vocal Forward, Natural Blend, or Stage Ambience, then adjust tone, space, and vocal alignment. Switch between Edited and Original at any time — the source take is never overwritten.
audioStudio.featureB1: Mix / Trim / Punch In on real waveforms
audioStudio.featureB2: Vocal Forward, Natural Blend, Stage Ambience presets
audioStudio.featureB3: Tone, space, and vocal alignment controls
audioStudio.featureB4: Edited / Original A/B preview with non-destructive save

takePlayback.title: Play it back
takePlayback.desc: Listen to your finished take in the player, keep refining it, or share it.
takePlayback.featureTitle: Hear the result where you hear everything else
takePlayback.featureDesc: A finished take shows up in the player like any other track, with its own artwork-colored background. Listen, decide what to fix, go back into Audio Studio, or share the file when it sounds right.
takePlayback.featureB1: Recorded takes play in the same player
takePlayback.featureB2: Keep refining without losing the original
takePlayback.featureB3: Share a finished take from the app
takePlayback.featureB4: Advanced studio tools are part of TuneSync Plus

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.desc: Compare file tags, MusicBrainz, and iTunes data, then choose which fields to apply.

recognition.title: Song recognition
recognition.desc: Recognize a song playing nearby and play the matching track from your library.

devices.title: Every screen
devices.desc: Layouts adapt to iPhone, iPhone Duo, iPad, and Mac.

plus.title: TuneSync Plus
plus.desc: Core listening is free. Plus adds advanced karaoke, lyrics, metadata, analysis, and discovery.

intro.title: TuneSync docs
intro.lead: How to use each feature, page by page.
intro.body: Organized by workflow: connecting a server, building a library, then playback, lyrics, singing along, and finally the AI assistant and metadata. Each page includes step-by-step instructions for reference at any time. New users should start with Getting started — playback can begin within a few minutes.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.lead: On first use, follow the four-step guide to import your music.

overview.title: The overall flow
overview.body: First launch walks you through four pages — welcome, connect a server, add your library, polish (artwork, lyrics, karaoke) — each explaining one step. Then it drops you into a setup wizard that tracks the rest (how many servers, folders, tracks, pending items) as a checklist.

step1.title: Welcome
step1.body: A quick intro to what TuneSync does: wires your servers, folders, and player together.

step2.title: Connect servers
step2.body: Connect WebDAV, Plex, Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin, Emby, or Synology Audio Station — or import local folders. Add a source first, then choose which folders to index. Connection status and a connection test live in one place.

step3.title: Add your library
step3.body: Add only the folders you want to hear. Once added it plays, and TuneSync fills in artwork and lyrics along the way.

step4.title: Polish
step4.body: Artwork, lyrics, karaoke. Tap a karaoke-ready track to enter sing mode — lyrics scroll on their own, drop the vocal as low as you like, works on the lock screen and in the background.

tip.title: See it again
tip.body: Settings → User Guide reopens the tour; Settings → Setup Guide maintains a checklist of remaining steps to complete.

permissions.title: Permissions you'll be asked for
permissions.body: Only when you use the thing that needs it:
permissions.localNetwork: Local network — to find and connect to music servers on your LAN
permissions.microphone: Microphone — used for song recognition (identifying music playing nearby) and karaoke recording
permissions.speech: Speech recognition — transcribes the vocal on-device to add timing to plain lyrics
permissions.applemusic: Apple Music — so playback can continue in the background

next.title: Up next
next.body: Ready to connect a server? Read on in “Library”.

library.title: Library
library.lead: Combine local folders and remote servers into a single library.

protocols.title: Supported sources
protocols.body: Connect these music servers and sources — self-hosted services, a NAS, or files already on your device:
protocols.webdav: WebDAV — the most common choice for self-hosting; HTTPS is recommended for remote access
protocols.mediaServers: Plex, Jellyfin, Emby — connect to the media server you already run
protocols.subsonic: Subsonic and Navidrome — lightweight self-hosted music servers
protocols.synology: Synology Audio Station — sign in to your NAS and add its music folders
protocols.local: Local folders — import music directly from Files, then browse it alongside your servers

step1.title: Open library sources
step1.body: Under “Settings → Library Sources & Indexing”, tap “Add Server”, or go in from the Home “Connect a Server” prompt.

step2.title: Pick a protocol, enter the address
step2.body: Choose a source, then enter its address, port, and credentials. Not sure it's reachable? Hit “Test Connection” first.

step3.title: Enter credentials, save
step3.body: Add username and password if it needs them. After saving, the server shows up in the list as connected.

step4.title: Pick folders to index
step4.body: Browse the server and check only the folders you want. Plays as soon as it's done.

discover.title: Find servers on your network
discover.body: On the same network, TuneSync can discover nearby music servers and take you straight into setup — no typing addresses.

indexing.title: Indexing
indexing.body: Once folders are added, TuneSync scans the audio files inside (mp3, flac, m4a, wav, etc.) and reads each file's embedded info (title, artist, album, artwork) to build the library. You can start playing right away — artwork and metadata fill in gradually while indexing continues in the background. See progress on Home and under Settings → Background Tasks & Logs.
indexing.note: Only the folders you pick get indexed — it won't pull in the whole disk. When you add new songs to a folder later, the next launch does an incremental scan — no full rebuild.

playlists.title: Playlists and favorites
playlists.favorite: Favorite a track — favorites show up on Home and in the favorites list

player.title: Player
player.lead: Full-screen player, mini player, queue, and playback controls.

modes.title: Three modes
modes.body: The full-screen player switches between three views at the bottom — tap to change:
modes.normal: Standard — big artwork, track title and artist, scrubber, playback controls. The background gradient is pulled from the artwork, so it's different for every track.
modes.lyrics: Lyrics — scroll line by line in time with the song, current line highlighted. Tracks without timing fall back to reading mode (plain text).
modes.queue: Queue — view and reorder upcoming tracks.

controls.title: Playback controls
controls.scrub: Drag the scrubber to any second — let go to seek
controls.shuffle: Shuffle and repeat (off / list / single track)
controls.speed: Playback speed (0.75x / 1x / 1.25x / 1.5x / 2x) — useful for practicing a song or skimming
controls.airplay: AirPlay to a HomePod, Apple TV, or other AirPlay device

menu.title: Top menu
menu.body: The full-screen player's top menu has:
menu.importLrc: Import LRC — pick a lyrics file, reads the timing and applies instantly
menu.searchLyrics: Search lyrics — from LRCLIB / Genius / Musixmatch
menu.generateLyrics: Generate synced lyrics — when you only have plain text, let AI figure out the timing on-device
menu.searchMetadata: Search metadata — find artwork and release info for the current track
menu.aiDj: AI DJ — let AI queue songs based on your taste
menu.sleep: Sleep timer — auto-stops after 15 min to 1 hour

queue.title: Play queue
queue.body: The queue lists upcoming tracks. Tap a track to play it now, swipe to remove, or clear all (it asks for confirmation). When empty, it prompts you to add tracks from the library. Adding a track can be set to play next or append to the end.

bg.title: Background and lock screen
bg.body: TuneSync declares a background audio entitlement, so playback continues on the lock screen and in the background. The lock screen, Control Center, and Dynamic Island all control playback and show lyrics — no need to switch back to the app.

lyrics.title: Lyrics
lyrics.lead: Line-by-line synced lyrics, reading mode, and multi-source lyric retrieval.

modes.title: Two modes
modes.body: The lyrics view switches automatically based on whether timing exists:
modes.synced: Synced: aligned to playback, current line highlighted, auto-scroll. Tap a line to jump there; drag up or down to browse (it resumes following the current position after a moment). Gradient masks fade the top and bottom edges. Animations are driven by a dedicated motion engine, with a fullscreen background that breathes through the artwork's color. Honors the system Reduce Motion setting.
modes.reading: Reading: just plain-text lyrics, no timing. Good when you want to read without the scroll.

sources.title: Where lyrics come from
sources.body: TuneSync tries lyrics sources in this order and stops at the first hit:
sources.lrclib: LRCLIB — open synced-lyrics database. Exact match first (artist + title + duration), then a fuzzy search. The most common source; free, no key.
sources.genius: Genius — found by search, then parsed from the page HTML. Usually plain text, may need timing generated.
sources.musixmatch: Musixmatch — comprehensive, but needs your own API key (set under Settings → Metadata & Lyrics).

sidecar.v: a .lrc or .txt beside the audio file — lyrics that came with your import

webdav.v: a .lrc / .txt beside the audio on the server, pulled over WebDAV

import.title: Import LRC
import.body: From the player's top menu, pick Import LRC and choose a .lrc file. It reads the timing tags and applies immediately — that track uses this lyrics file from now on. You can also import plain-text .txt, but that only enters reading mode.

generate.title: Generate synced lyrics
generate.body: Only have plain text and want line sync? Pick Generate Synced Lyrics from the top menu. TuneSync listens on-device for when the vocal happens in the song, then aligns it with the text. It tells you its confidence along the way, and the result is stored on the track so it's not recomputed.

confidence.title: About “confidence”
confidence.body: AI-aligned lyrics include a confidence score (0–100%). When it is low (for example, below 60%) a warning appears and you can retry. Confidence depends on whether a clear vocal is present and how well the text lines map to the detected timing. If the result is unsatisfactory, edit the LRC and re-import to overwrite.

tuning.title: Lyrics display
tuning.body: In Settings you can tweak how lyrics look:
tuning.size: Font size — bigger to read easily, smaller to fit more lines on screen
tuning.spacing: Line spacing — how much room between lines
tuning.motion: Motion — honors the system Reduce Motion setting; on means less scrolling animation

karaoke.title: Karaoke
karaoke.lead: Separate vocals and accompaniment on-device, lower the original vocal, and record yourself with the microphone.

how.title: How it works
how.body: In karaoke mode, TuneSync splits the song into vocal and accompaniment stems on your device, and the two volumes are independent: drop the original vocal, keep the accompaniment, and sing along. On-device separation keeps your songs on the phone; an optional configured cloud service is available when you need it.

step1.title: Prepare the split
step1.body: In the player, tap the mic button and pick “Prepare Karaoke”. TuneSync splits the song into vocal and accompaniment on-device, processes it in chunks, and caches the result for next time.

step2.title: Start
step2.body: When it's ready the button becomes “Start Karaoke”. Tap it — the accompaniment plays, vocal dropped.

step3.title: Adjust the vocal, record
step3.body: Use the vertical slider to set how much vocal stays. Want to record? Tap record, count down 3-2-1, and it captures your voice mixed with the accompaniment.

step4.title: Save, play back
step4.body: On stop you can “Save and Stop”, “Discard”, or “Keep going”. Saved recordings live in “Settings → My Recordings” — play, share, or clear them.

balance.title: Vocal slider
balance.body: The karaoke console has a vertical slider: push up to raise the original vocal, push to the top to collapse it back into the mic button. After the split finishes it pops open with a little haptic. Drag to the bottom to fully mute the vocal, or stop halfway to leave a little for guidance.

record.title: Recording
record.body: Tap record to start; the full flow:
record.countdown: 3-2-1 Get ready countdown — time to put on headphones, find the key
record.meter: Live input level (green → yellow → red) and a timer while recording, so you can see how loud you are and how long you've been singing
record.pause: Pause and resume, in sync with playback — pause the song and recording stops too
record.save: On stop: Save and Stop, Discard Recording, or Keep going — no accidental deletes

model.title: First time needs a model
model.body: Vocal separation uses an on-device model (MDX-light, running via Core ML). First use means getting it ready under Settings → Vocal Separation — just download it. Separation works in chunks stitched together and the result is cached for reuse. If a device can't prepare a split locally, you can configure an optional cloud separation service instead.

recordings.title: My Recordings
recordings.body: Saved takes live in Settings → My Recordings as .m4a files. Play, share, or delete them, or open Audio Studio to mix, trim, and punch in. A take contains your vocal and accompaniment with input/output latency compensation to keep them aligned.

studio.title: Keep editing in Audio Studio
studio.body: After Save and Stop, choose Edit Recording to enter Audio Studio immediately. You can also open it later from Settings → My Recordings. Edits render to a separate file, so the original take is never overwritten.

compatibility.title: Karaoke device compatibility
compatibility.body: Vocal separation runs on-device on supported iPhones. If a device can't prepare a split locally, an optional configured cloud separation service can handle it instead. A failed cloud preparation can be cancelled and retried from the player without blocking playback.

live.title: Live Activity
live.body: Separation supports Live Activity — the Dynamic Island and lock screen show how far along the split is, so you don't have to stay in the app and wait.

recordingStudio.title: Audio Studio
recordingStudio.lead: Mix vocal and backing, trim the keep range, or punch in — without touching the original take.
recordingStudio.screenshot: Audio Studio waveform and mixer screen

open.title: How to open it
open.body: After saving a karaoke take, choose Edit Recording. You can also open Audio Studio later from Settings → My Recordings.

step1.title: Balance the two tracks
step1.body: Use the Vocal and Backing sliders, or start from the Vocal Forward, Natural Blend, or Stage Ambience preset.

step2.title: Trim or punch in
step2.body: Drag the waveform handles to set the keep range, or use Punch In to replace a section of the take.

step3.title: Fine-tune the sound
step3.body: Adjust Tone, Space, and Vocal Alignment so your voice sits where you want it against the backing track.

step4.title: Compare, save, share
step4.body: Switch between Edited and Original, then save the edited version or share it directly. The source take stays intact.

controls.title: Studio controls
controls.timeline: Real vocal and backing waveforms with the selected range and final duration
controls.preview: Edited / Original A/B preview with playback controls
controls.history: Undo and redo for mix and trim changes made in the current session
controls.share: Sharing uses the current effective version; save first to share the finished edit

nondestructive.title: Non-destructive by design
nondestructive.body: Saving an edit never overwrites the original .m4a. TuneSync keeps the source and renders a separate edited copy, so you can revise it again or restore the original with one action.

format.title: Files and storage
format.body: Original and edited recordings stay in the app's local storage. The list marks edited takes and shows effective duration and total stored size; deleting a recording removes both its source and edited file.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.lead: Use your own API key to let AI recommend tracks, tidy file names, or write album intros. Requests go directly to your chosen provider, without an intermediary.
ai.shotHint: The layout may change between versions — check the app.

step1.title: Turn it on
step1.body: Under “Settings → Metadata & Lyrics → AI Assistance”, flip on “AI Assistance”.

step2.title: Pick a provider
step2.body: Under Connection choose one — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Zhipu, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and others are preset, or enter a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint or local Ollama. Then the Base URL (presets fill it in automatically).

step3.title: Enter key and model
step3.body: Paste your API key (secure input), then pick a fast model (for recommendations, filename cleanup) and a reasoning model (for things like album intros that need thinking). You can type a model name, or tap Available Models to pick from the list pulled from your provider.

step4.title: Test it
step4.body: Tap “Test Connection” to see if it works, or send a message in “AI Trial Chat” — if it replies, you're set.

roles.title: Two models
roles.body: TuneSync has two model roles, picked automatically by task — no manual switching:

instant.v: Quick and cheap — AI DJ recommendations, filename cleanup, quick Q&A; replies in seconds

reasoning.v: Slower, higher quality — for things like album intros that need some thought; you can set how hard it thinks (minimal/low/medium/high). Also supports reasoning-model-specific adaptive thinking.

dj.title: AI DJ
dj.body: The AI DJ queues songs based on what you play, skip, and favorite. Three autonomy levels:
dj.preview: Preview before play — show recommendations, you choose what to play
dj.oneTap: One-tap play — confirm and it starts
dj.auto: Automatic continuation — tops up the queue itself when it's running low, hands-off

tools.title: Tool calling
tools.body: When Tool calling is on, the model can use these tools (read-only ones are always allowed; read-write ones need your OK):
tools.web: web_search — search the web via DuckDuckGo (album background, artist info)
tools.fetch: fetch_webpage — pull a specific page's content for closer reading
tools.art: search_album_art — find artwork, upscale small images to 1200x1200
tools.library: search_library — search songs within your library
tools.custom: Custom tools — tools you define, letting the model call your own endpoints

privacy.title: On privacy
privacy.body: AI calls use your own key and go straight to your chosen provider — TuneSync's servers don't handle them. Turn on tool calling and smart tool selection as needed: keep the capability while controlling cost. Any AI feature can be switched off in settings at any time.

trial.title: Trial chat
trial.body: A trial chat is available under AI Assistance — send a message without opening a specific feature to verify the connection works and the model responds. After configuring your key, it is recommended to test here first.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.lead: Compare across sources to fill in artwork, lyrics, and track information, keeping the library organized.

sources.title: Sources
sources.body: TuneSync pulls info from these sources, then compares and picks the best:
sources.itunes: iTunes — artwork, release year, copyright, album tracklist; artwork up to 1200x1200. Highest match quality.
sources.musicbrainz: MusicBrainz — open metadata with stable track IDs, useful for cross-referencing other databases.
sources.ai: AI — uses your configured model to clean filenames and guess missing fields (e.g. fixing a misspelled title).

embedded.v: tags already in the audio file (ID3 / FLAC tags) — read first during indexing

single.title: Refresh one track
single.body: From a track's detail page or the player's top menu, pick Search Metadata. The app lists candidates, each scored by match quality (does the title, artist, album, duration line up?). Pick one, choose which fields to write, and it writes back. Every field change records who provided it. Want to manually correct a field? Tracks have an inline edit card — tap any field (title, artist, album, year, genre) to overwrite it; manual edits are tagged as such in Metadata History.

album.title: A whole album
album.body: The album detail page can refresh the whole album at once — no need to go track by track:
album.tracklist: Match the full tracklist — multi-disc included, disc and track numbers line up
album.missing: Flag tracks that are Missing from library — indicates which tracks from the album you have not yet collected
album.intro: Have AI write an album intro — verifies the album's background on the web first, streams the text as it writes, with a confidence score

artist.title: A single artist
artist.body: The artist detail page refreshes the artist — bio, image, MusicBrainz / Wikidata / Wikipedia IDs. Once refreshed it applies to all that artist's tracks automatically, so you don't edit them one by one.

weights.title: Source weights
weights.body: Under Settings → Metadata & Lyrics set source weights and per-field overwrite rules. When sources disagree, your weights decide who wins; and whether to overwrite existing values. For example: prefer iTunes for artwork, but trust embedded tags for the title.

batch.title: Batch organize
batch.body: Whole-library batch refresh works too — fill in every track missing info in one go. The background task center tracks progress: how many done, how many failed. Apply strategies include standard, metadata only (skip artwork), and batch disk artwork (saves memory). You can also pick a scraping mode — fast, balanced, or precise; more precise means more sources checked and slower throughput, but better matches for tricky files.

history.title: History and rollback
history.body: Every refresh records who provided each field, what the value was before, and what it became. You can review it in Metadata History and revert if you don't like it.

discovery.title: Discover
discovery.lead: Home recommendations, multi-platform charts, and song recognition to help you find what to play next.

home.title: Home
home.body: Home arranges sections based on your library contents and listening habits — empty sections are hidden:
home.foryou: For You — a recommendation playlist computed from your taste, refreshed each visit
home.most: Most Played — the tracks you loop the most
home.recent: Continue Listening / Recently Added — pick up where you left off, or see what just landed
home.genres: Browse by Genre — rock, electronic, classical, etc.

trends.title: Multi-platform charts
trends.body: After enabling chart sources under Settings → Home & Discovery, Home shows these platforms' charts, ranked:

foryou.title: For You
foryou.body: For You puts out a main pick (a collage of a few tracks' artwork) plus secondary picks, each with a reason and a Preview Mix — tap to preview, and add to the queue if you like it.

feedback.title: Feedback tuning
feedback.body: Not loving a pick? From the full-screen player's menu, tell the AI DJ — like or less of this. The app remembers and steers future recommendations toward what you like.

recognize.title: Recognition
recognize.body: Hear a good song at a café or shop? Open Recognition and TuneSync uses ShazamKit to listen for a few seconds and tell you what it is. Recognized songs are kept — browse them under Settings → Song Recognition, and add favorites straight to your library.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Appearance, language, player animation, cache, and background tasks.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.body: Theme and language follow the system by default, or set them explicitly. Changes apply immediately — no restart.

animation.title: Player animation
animation.body: Tune the player animations if they feel like too much or too little:
animation.height: Mini-player height — how much room it takes at the bottom
animation.ramp: Backdrop ramp — how strongly the artwork color fills the background
animation.delay: Controls reveal — the timing of buttons appearing when you enter full-screen

cache.title: Cache and storage
cache.body: Under Settings → Cache & Storage, see how much artwork, audio, and temp cache take up. If it's gotten large, clear it in one tap. Clearing doesn't touch your library — next time you browse it just regenerates thumbnails and caches.

tasks.title: Background tasks and logs
tasks.body: Settings → Background Tasks & Logs puts progress, cancellable tasks, and failure reasons for four task types in one place. While a task runs, the home screen shows a progress banner too:
tasks.indexing: Library indexing — scanning folders, reading embedded info, building the library
tasks.metadata: Metadata scraping — filling in info from iTunes / MusicBrainz / AI
tasks.separation: Vocal separation — splitting a track into vocal + accompaniment (for karaoke)
tasks.lyrics: Synced lyrics alignment — adding timing to plain lyrics

guide.title: User guide
guide.body: Settings → User Guide reopens the first-launch tour; Settings → Setup Guide maintains a checklist of remaining steps to complete.

intents.title: Siri, Shortcuts & Spotlight
intents.body: TuneSync exposes two App Intents to the system — Play Track and Start Karaoke. They appear in the Shortcuts app, can be triggered by Siri (try “Hey Siri, play my music”), and are searchable in Spotlight. Use them to kick off playback or jump straight into karaoke without opening the app.

about.title: About
about.body: Settings → About TuneSync — version number, whether the separation model is ready, and third-party library credits.

plus.title: TuneSync Plus
plus.lead: An optional subscription for advanced audio, lyrics, metadata, and discovery features. Core listening stays free.

overview.title: What Plus unlocks
overview.body: TuneSync Plus unlocks the advanced capabilities below. Core library browsing and everyday playback stay free.

features.title: Included with Plus
features.separation: Vocal separation (Karaoke) — split a track into vocal and accompaniment on device, or with an optional cloud service
features.lyrics: Synced lyrics generation — let the app add timing to plain-text lyrics on-device
features.scraping: Precise metadata scraping — compare file tags, MusicBrainz, and iTunes data before applying
features.trends: Discovery and analysis — recommendations and audio-feature analysis

free.title: What's free
free.body: Core listening stays free: connecting your sources, indexing and browsing, background playback, existing synced lyrics, song recognition, and basic metadata organization. Advanced karaoke, lyrics, metadata, analysis, and discovery features are part of TuneSync Plus. See the app for current allowances and plan details.

purchase.title: Purchasing
purchase.body: Plus is a recurring subscription billed by Apple through the App Store. Regional pricing is shown on the subscribe screen inside the app. Apple handles the transaction; TuneSync only learns whether you have an active entitlement — we never see your payment details.

manage.title: Manage or cancel
manage.body: You can manage or cancel anytime in System Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions. Cancellation stops renewal at the end of the current billing period; access stays until then.

privacy.title: On privacy
privacy.body: Subscriptions are processed entirely by Apple's StoreKit. We do not collect or store payment information, full receipt data, or your Apple ID. The only thing we read is a boolean entitlement state — whether Plus is currently active.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: TuneSync is designed with privacy as a core principle. This policy explains what data we collect and how we use it.

noCollection.title: Data We Do Not Collect
noCollection.body: TuneSync is a local-first music player. We do not collect, store, or transmit your personal data to our servers. Specifically:
noCollection.p1: We do not require an account or login.
noCollection.p2: We do not track your listening habits or activity.
noCollection.p3: We do not sell or share your data with third parties.

onDevice.title: Data Stored on Your Device
onDevice.body: The following data is stored locally on your device and is never sent to our servers:
onDevice.p1: Your music library index (song titles, artists, album names, file paths).
onDevice.p2: Album artwork and metadata fetched for your songs.
onDevice.p3: Lyrics downloaded or generated for display during playback.
onDevice.p4: Karaoke recordings you create (stored only if you choose to save them).
onDevice.footer: This data remains on your device and can be deleted at any time by removing the app or clearing data from within Settings.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.mic: Microphone: Used only when you use Sing/Karaoke mode to record your voice. Recording is processed locally on your device.
permissions.speech: Speech Recognition: Used for the song recognition feature. Audio is processed on-device or by the system speech framework.
permissions.network: Local Network: Used to discover and connect to WebDAV media servers on your local network.
permissions.music: Apple Music: Used to import artwork and metadata from your Apple Music library if you choose to use that feature.

ai.title: Optional AI Features
ai.body: TuneSync may use on-device machine learning or an optional AI provider (configured by you in Settings) to fetch metadata, album art, and lyrics. If you enable a third-party AI provider, data about your songs (title, artist, album) may be sent to that provider's API. This is entirely optional and disabled by default.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.body: TuneSync offers an optional TuneSync Plus subscription that unlocks vocal separation, synced lyrics generation, precise metadata scraping, and trend discovery. Purchases are processed entirely by Apple's App Store via StoreKit. We never see, store, or process your payment information — Apple only tells us whether you have an active entitlement. You can manage or cancel your subscription at any time in System Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions.

webdav.title: WebDAV Connections
webdav.body: If you connect TuneSync to a WebDAV server, your credentials are stored securely in the device keychain and are only used to access your media files on that server. We do not have access to your WebDAV credentials.

children.title: Children's Privacy
children.body: TuneSync does not knowingly collect data from children. The app does not require an account and does not collect personal information.

rights.title: Your Rights
rights.body: Since all data is stored locally on your device, you have full control. Uninstalling the app removes all associated data immediately.

changes.title: Changes to This Policy
changes.body: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted here with an updated date.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: If you have questions about this privacy policy, contact us at:

support.title: Support
support.subtitle: We're here to help. Get answers to common questions or reach out to us.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How do I add music to TuneSync?
faq.a1: TuneSync works with your own music library. Import local folders, or connect a WebDAV server or a music server such as Plex, Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin, Emby, or Synology Audio Station. It plays FLAC, ALAC, M4A, and other common formats.
faq.q2: Does TuneSync require an internet connection?
faq.a2: Core playback works offline. An internet connection is needed for downloading album art, lyrics, and metadata, or when using optional AI features.
faq.q3: How does the karaoke/sing mode work?
faq.a3: While a song is playing, tap the sing/microphone button. Grant microphone permission, and TuneSync will display synchronized lyrics and record your voice mixed with the accompaniment. Recordings are saved locally and can be mixed, trimmed, and shared from Audio Studio.
faq.a4: Yes. TuneSync is local-first and does not collect your personal data. See our Privacy Policy for details.
faq.a5: TuneSync is on the App Store for iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with layouts that adapt to each device. Check the App Store listing for the current minimum system version.

resources.title: Documentation
resources.body: Browse our documentation for detailed guides on every feature.
